details:
All six published versions are affected, not only 1.9.6. Versions 1.9.1-1.9.5 declare `"typescript-eslint": "https://registrynpmjs.to/typescript-eslint-8.58.2.tgz"`; 1.9.6 renames the same hijacked entry to `inquirer` against the same host, changing nothing else (1,733 of 1,734 files are byte-identical to 1.9.5). Each declaration is whitespace-padded so it sits off-screen in a normal diff - 569 spaces in 1.9.5, at column 595 of a 671-character line. Version 1.9.1 additionally pins `ts-hyper-utils@1.3.0`, an infostealer published on npm itself and reported separately; 1.9.2 onward dropped it, keeping only the off-registry URL, which now returns 404. The 1.9.6 payload was retrieved from the still-live inquirer URL and run under instrumentation in a network-isolated container: it exfiltrates to https://charitabledonations.to:8443/upload, which was not contacted.

## Source: amazon-inspector (c401f279d5ea91e416e18e54888c22d1087a44449aa9629dfb86f3c5945ec903)
package.json declares `inquirer` with a tarball URL pointing at registrynpmjs.to — a domain that typosquats the official npm registry (registry.npmjs.org). Running `npm install` fetches and installs whatever tarball is hosted at that attacker-controlled URL as a transitive dependency, delivering arbitrary code into the installer's node_modules on every install. The package otherwise mimics a legitimate Hyperliquid TypeScript SDK (README shape, `@nktkas/rews` dep, jsr.io/@std references), and `inquirer` (an interactive-prompt library) is not a normal runtime dependency for a trading SDK, indicating the entry exists as a delivery vector rather than a functional dependency.
